name: Answer staff questions from SOPs and policies
summary: Turns a staff question into a reply grounded in the business's own SOPs and policies, in the thread it came from. Crons read, search and draft; a person approves every reply before it goes out.

covered_by.question-arrives: intake (Gmail, a Chat space, a Slack channel)
covered_by.answer-staff: skill writes the answer, draft queues the reply for approval
covered_by.escalate: register (a question with no matching source is parked for a person)

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: New staff questions from Gmail, a Chat space and a Slack channel.

crons.name: draft
crons.summary: Find SOP sources for each question; where an answer is written, draft the reply and queue its send for approval.

crons.name: register
crons.summary: One row per question in the question register Sheet.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads, a Gmail draft of a reply, a row in the question register. Sending a reply is a live operation and waits for a person.

google-workspace.covers: Gmail and Chat questions, Drive SOP search, Gmail reply drafts, Chat replies, the question register Sheet

slack.covers: channel questions, file search, replies in the question's thread

gaps: Confluence holds SOPs, but no platform help docs for it were read, so it has no adapter yet.
Microsoft 365: the help pages read are Word and Windows accessibility guides, so nothing supports this workflow. Its operations are mapped in the kit but no adapter was built.
No runtime command writes an answer into the store. The agent skill needs an answer command in tools/workflow.ts (a core change) before a reply can be queued from a real question.
Slack file search needs a user token with search:read. Confirm the scope before the first live run.
The question register logs each question once, at the status it has then. A later reply is not written back to its row.
update-sop, publish-update and onboarding-pointer are not covered: they are judgment or document-owner steps, and the platform help pages do not describe them.
Every adapter is docs-only until a sandbox Google Workspace account and a Slack test workspace prove it.
